model: Life insurer FCFE at cost of equity, net debt held at zero (engine route)

equity_bridge.item: Remaining GBP600M of the 2026 buyback (tranche 2, 14 Sept 2026 - c. Mar 2027), funded by Meiji Yasuda sale capital already in SII own funds
equity_bridge.note: H1 2026 interim: full GBP1.2bn buyback recognised up-front in own funds; tranche 1 GBP600M completed 11 Sept 2026. This capital exists today and is not generated by the flows being capitalised, so it is added once here; the share count is NOT also reduced for it, which would double-count.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: midpoint of the business operating-profit CAGR targets (Institutional Retirement 5-7% 2023-28, Retail 4-6% 2024-28, Asset Management to GBP500-600M by 2028 from 402), cross-checked against the FY2021-FY2025 DPS CAGR of 4.2% (18.45p -> 21.79p), FY2025 OSG per share +8% and diluted core operating EPS +8.9% (18.40p -> 20.03p). Equity and EPS CAGRs are accounting artefacts and are not used.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr/5yr CAGRs (-29%/-28%) are artefacts: IFRS 17 cut FY2022 equity from 11,673 to a restated 5,067, and since then dividends plus buybacks (GBP1.75bn in FY2025) have exceeded IFRS net income, which itself is depressed by investment variances (FY2023 457, FY2024 191, FY2025 592). Reported EPS 3yr/5yr CAGRs are undefined for the same reason (FY2022 38.3p IFRS 4 -> FY2025 10.0p IFRS 17). No owner-FCF series exists for an insurer, so FCF CAGRs are null. Revenue CAGRs are mildly negative because FY2025 excludes the sold US business while FY2020-FY2024 include it.

scenario_narratives.base: A UK retirement-and-asset-management flywheel paying out most of what it earns. Core operating profit compounds at ~6% to FY2028, roughly the midpoint of management's segment targets, then fades; after 25% tax and a 5-10% retention for new-business strain, the FCFE stream is capitalised at a 10.5% GBP cost of equity with the terminal capped at 11x. The remaining GBP600M of the Meiji-funded buyback is added once as surplus capital. The result is modestly above the price: the market is paying for a ~7.6% dividend yield growing 2% and little else.
scenario_narratives.bull: Everything on the 2028 scorecard is delivered: Asset Management at GBP600M, PRT volumes recover with share held at the IRR hurdle, asset optimisation stays above GBP400M, the cost programme sticks, strain stays near 1% so conversion reaches 100%, and the stock rerates to 12x FCFE.
scenario_narratives.bear: Pricing discipline costs share permanently, LGIM fee compression wins, asset optimisation normalises lower, restructuring disappoints and Pillar II lifts tax; the stock settles at 9x a slower-growing FCFE stream.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value a life insurer on the cash it can distribute to shareholders, not on IFRS net income (dominated by investment variance under IFRS 17) and not on OCF (policyholder flows). Core operating profit after the standard tax rate is L&G's own measure of distributable earnings and is what the dividend is paid from; management's Solvency II surplus-generation commentary sets how much of it must be retained. Debt interest is already inside that earnings measure, so net debt is zero in the bridge. The one-off Meiji Yasuda capital that funds the remaining buyback is added once. Historical growth from the CSV is unusable across the IFRS 17 transition and the US disposal, so the forward paths are built from management's segment targets, haircut for the H1 2026 evidence of PRT competition.
key_risks_to_valuation: PRT competition: Rothesay (c.28%) overtook L&G (c.18%) in H1 2026; sustained share loss slows back-book growth and LGIM flow-through -- the bear path

Rate/credit-spread sensitivity of the GBP91bn annuity portfolio: IFRS earnings and SII own funds both move with gilts and spreads (H1 2026 took GBP344M of adverse economic variance below core operating profit)
Longevity assumption changes on a long-duration back book
Solvency UK / matching-adjustment regime changes and Pillar II (Bermuda deferred tax asset unwind from 2027)
LGIM fee compression on the GBP1.2tn index/LDI-heavy AUM base; Asset Management target of GBP500-600M by 2028 depends on the Private Markets mix shift
Execution of the 1,000-role restructuring announced Sept 2026
Model risk: the valuation assumes 90-95% of after-tax core earnings is distributable; if new-business strain structurally exceeds the SII release from the back book, FCFE is lower than modelled

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (LSE regular close); 52-week range 217.2-318.1p
data_sources.financials: LGEN.L_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, GBP millions, FY2017-FY2025 + H1 FY2025/H1 FY2026); FY2025 Annual Report (core operating profit by segment, Note 34 share-based payments, core operating EPS note, borrowings, SII own funds analysis); H1 2026 Interim Management Report (SII capital table, OSG/NSG, share capital note, segment table, tax); H1 2026 results presentation (asset optimisation guidance)
data_sources.qualitative: LGEN.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10): PRT competition, Meiji Yasuda divestiture, GBP1.2bn buyback, Solvency II regime, Sept 2026 restructuring

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 continuing-operations top line as the CSV defines revenue: IFRS 17 insurance revenue 9,222 + fee income 908 + other operational income 381 = 10,511 (FY2025 AR consolidated income statement). FY2024's 12,642 still contains the US protection/PRT business sold to Meiji Yasuda (completed 2 Feb 2026, discontinued from FY2025), so FY2025 is the first clean base. H1 2026 was 5,730 (5,105 + 516 + 109) vs H1 2025 5,055. Insurance revenue is largely CSM/risk-adjustment release plus expected claims on the back book, so it grows with the in-force book rather than with new-business premiums; the margin on it is the core operating margin, not an EBITDA in any operating-company sense.
inputs.share_count_basis: 5,541.4M ordinary shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 interim, share capital note: 5,697.6M at 1 Jan 2026 less 159.5M cancelled under the buyback plus 3.3M options exercised). The first GBP600M buyback tranche completed on 11 Sept 2026 having bought 225.5M shares in total, so a further 66.0M were cancelled after the balance-sheet date: 5,475.4M issued at 11 Sept 2026. Plus ~25M of option/award dilution (diluted weighted average 5,940M vs basic ~5,671M in H1 2026 is mostly the RT1 notes, see below) = 5,500M. The GBP495M restricted Tier 1 notes are NOT treated as dilutive: their coupon sits inside Group debt costs, which is already deducted in core operating profit, so the flows pay for them. Held FLAT thereafter: SBC is charged in the flows, and the second GBP600M tranche is carried in equity_bridge rather than as a share-count reduction (see bridge note). Employee-scheme treasury shares are immaterial (<0.3%).
inputs.net_debt_treatment: Held at ZERO, the banks/insurers convention. Total borrowings GBP5,023M at 30 June 2026 = core borrowings 4,310 (Tier 2 subordinated and senior) + operational borrowings 713 (non-recourse / matched funding). Core debt interest is Group debt costs (GBP229M FY2025, GBP114M H1 2026, 5.0% average cost) and is deducted INSIDE core operating profit; operational borrowings are matched by the assets they fund. Deducting debt again would count it twice. Consolidated cash GBP14,517M is overwhelmingly policyholder and matching-portfolio liquidity, not shareholder surplus. The GBP6.5bn Solvency II surplus (201% coverage vs 160-190% target) is the regulatory buffer that lets the business write PRT and is not added back, with one exception recorded in equity_bridge.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 diluted core operating earnings after tax, GBP1,217M = core operating profit 1,623 x (1 - 25% standard UK rate), per the core operating EPS note (20.03p diluted on 6,076M shares). Used as the observed FCFE proxy: FY2025 dividends paid GBP1,247M were ~102% of it, with the GBP503M FY2025 buyback funded separately by disposals, and FY2025 Solvency II operational surplus generation (OSG, +5% YoY; H1 2026 GBP790M, NSG GBP713M after GBP77M new-business strain) running above IFRS core earnings because SII releases back-book capital. Management's own cover statement (SII NSG to cover the dividend by 2027 under normal strain) is why conversion is set BELOW 100% in the near years. An insurer's OCF-less-capex (CSV OCF +4,548 FY2025, -3,034 H1 2026) is policyholder flow, not free cash, so the identity last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income is deliberately not satisfied.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR Note 34 Share-based payments: total expense GBP71M (FY2024 72, FY2023 59), all equity-settled. The IFRS 2 charge is already inside core operating profit, so ebitda_margin_path is stated PRE-SBC (core operating profit + 71 = 1,694 / 10,511 = 16.1%) and SBC is then charged explicitly at 0.68% of revenue; net effect equals core operating profit, and the house/street band stays meaningful. No net-share-settlement withholding is disclosed; the EquityAwardTaxes KPI is 0.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 GBP503M (203.4M shares cancelled); FY2024 GBP201M; H1 2026 GBP411M (159.5M shares). The 2026 programme is GBP1.2bn in two GBP600M tranches: tranche 1 ran 12 Mar - 11 Sept 2026 (225.5M shares at 266.07p average), tranche 2 started 14 Sept 2026 to run to c. March 2027. The programme was explicitly funded by the c. GBP1.2bn of SII capital released by the Meiji Yasuda sale, not by the ongoing surplus the model capitalises.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows are GBP millions; the LSE quote is pence sterling. fx_rate converts model to quote: 1 GBP = 100 GBp, a fixed denomination ratio, not a market rate, so no date or source applies and no parity check is possible (L&G has no US ADR; the OTC LGGNY line is illiquid). Canonical intrinsic_value, weighted_iv and entry_price are therefore in GBp and comparable to current_price; *_gbp siblings hold pounds per share.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T15:49:17Z LSE closing auction (regular close, Friday); 52-week range 217.2-318.1p
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-09-11 (30 June 2026 note roll-forward adjusted for the post-period completion of buyback tranche 1)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of EQUITY 10.5%, built in GBP because the flows are GBP: UK 10-year gilt ~4.6% (early Oct 2026, approximate; no live gilt quote is available through the Yahoo chart endpoint) + beta ~1.15 x 5.0% ERP = ~10.3%, rounded up to 10.5%. The beta premium over a UK bank reflects a leveraged spread balance sheet (SII debt leverage 33.9%, GBP91bn annuity portfolio) whose IFRS earnings carry two-sided rate, credit-spread and longevity sensitivity. Same 10.5% as HSBA.L (USD-built) and 0.5pp above PRU's 10.0% USD rate, consistent with the ~0.3-0.4pp gilt-over-Treasury gap. One rate across all three scenarios; risk is carried in the bear path and its 25% weight.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: lease liabilities GBP75M net at FY2025 (FY2025 AR lease note), and the IFRS 16 charge sits inside the operating expense base already deducted in core operating profit.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are GBP24-29M of profit in FY2025, a trivial share of consolidated private-markets vehicles; core operating profit is stated after them and no further deduction is made.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity on a UK life insurer / pensions / asset manager, run through the component engine with net debt at zero -- the PRU / MET / GL / IAG.AX pattern in this folder (SKILL.md routing row: insurer). Not the owner-FCF DCF: OCF swings from +20bn to -14bn on policyholder flows and EBITDA does not exist. Not the pure BVPS x exit-P/B route either: IFRS 17 shareholders' equity (GBP1.8bn FY2025, 2.2bn H1 2026) is tiny against a GBP13.0bn CSM+RA store of future profit and GBP12.9bn of SII own funds, so book value is not where the value sits and the H1 2026 operating ROE of 70% says the same thing. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = insurance revenue + fee income + other operational income; ebitda_margin_path = core operating profit before SBC as % of revenue; sbc_pct_path = IFRS 2 charge; da = 0; cash_tax_rate = 25% standard UK rate (the rate L&G itself allocates to core operating EPS; equity holders' ETR FY2025 24%); capex_pct_path is the RETENTION plug = the share of after-tax core earnings kept as new-business strain and growth capital, so FCFE conversion = 1 - capex/(after-tax core earnings). FISCAL BASIS: FY0 = FY2025 (Dec), the first year on a continuing (ex-US) basis; FY2022 and earlier in the CSV are IFRS 4 (net income, equity) while FY2023+ are IFRS 17, so no series spanning FY2022 is used as an anchor -- the base is FY2025 core operating profit and H1 2026 run-rate. SURPLUS CAPITAL: SII 201% vs 160-190% target is roughly GBP0.7-1.3bn above the top of the range before the remaining buyback; only the GBP600M remaining tranche-2 capital (Meiji-funded, committed) is added in equity_bridge; the balance is treated as the regulatory buffer that supports PRT writing. Corporate Investments run-off (~GBP500M assets remaining, proceeds to buybacks) is NOT added -- conservative by up to ~9p/share.
inputs.transition_note: FY2022 row carries old-basis IFRS 4 net income (2,291) and equity (11,673) against an IFRS 17-restated OCF; the IFRS 17 restated FY2022 equity was 5,067 (KPI ShareholdersEquityIFRS17Restated). FY2023 net income 457 and FY2024 191 are IFRS 17 and depressed by investment variances and the US business; none of FY2021-FY2024 is used as an earnings anchor.

bear.narrative: Rothesay and PIC keep pricing below L&G's 14% IRR hurdle, so UK PRT share stays near the 18% of H1 2026 and the back book (and LGIM flow-through) grows more slowly; LGIM's index/LDI fee compression outruns the Private Markets mix shift and the GBP500-600M target slips past 2028; asset optimisation falls back toward the old GBP300M guidance as spreads tighten; the 1,000-role programme costs more and delivers later than planned. Pre-SBC margin erodes to 14.5% by FY2029 (core operating profit flat-to-down in real terms). Rising strain as PRT scales keeps FCFE conversion at 85%, below management's dividend-cover path, and Bermuda Pillar II lifts the tax rate to 26% from 2027 per the FY2025 and H1 2026 tax notes. Terminal min(Gordon 10.5%/2%, 9x) -- a UK-life multiple in a derating.

base.narrative: FY2026: revenue +8% (H1 +13% YoY on the continuing base, H2 slower against a stronger H2 2025) at a flat 16.1% pre-SBC margin gives core operating profit ~GBP1.75bn (+8%; H1 918 +7%, asset optimisation guidance raised to >GBP400M p.a. with GBP288M already in H1), which with ~4% fewer shares is core operating EPS growth above the 9% top of the range, as guided. FY2027-28: +6% p.a. as Asset Management climbs toward GBP500-600M by 2028, Institutional Retirement and Retail run at the middle of their 5-7% / 4-6% ranges and Group investment projects shrink with the 1,000-role programme (margin to 16.4%); core operating profit ~GBP1.96bn in FY2028. Thereafter fading to 2.5% by FY2034-35 as the UK PRT market matures. FCFE conversion 90% (FY2026) -> 92% -> 95% from FY2028 as SII NSG covers the dividend by 2027 per management; the residual 5% is permanent new-business strain. Tax 25%. Terminal min(Gordon 10.5%/2.5%, 11x FCFE) -- the cap binds, at the upper end of where UK life insurers have traded on earnings.

bull.narrative: The 2028 plan lands in full: Asset Management reaches GBP600M (fee margin into double-digit bps, cost-income below 70%, Private Markets past GBP85bn), the UK PRT market reverts to GBP45-50bn+ with deferred 2026 deals landing in 2027 and L&G holding ~20% share at its 14% IRR hurdle, asset optimisation runs above GBP400M with credit-spread upside, and the restructuring takes ~GBP150M out of the cost base. Pre-SBC margin to 17.2% by FY2029 (core operating profit ~GBP2.2bn FY2028). The sovereigns-based day-one strategy keeps strain near 1%, so FCFE conversion reaches 100% from FY2028 and the SII ratio drifts down to the 190% top of range funding further buybacks from flows. Terminal min(Gordon 10.5%/3%, 12x).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 11x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the loss of UK PRT leadership to Rothesay in H1 2026 is a live, not hypothetical, competitive shift; a 34%-levered annuity balance sheet has asymmetric downside in a rate-and-credit downturn; and the Solvency II ratio is guided to drift down from 201% toward the 160-190% range. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things together -- Asset Management at the top of its range, PRT share recovery without conceding on IRR, 100% conversion the company has not yet demonstrated, and a rerating. Same 25/50/25 as PRU and MET, the closest life-insurer comparables in this folder.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
